summary: Flags comparisons where either operand is exactly the literal value '-0'.
fixDescription: Replaces every occurrence of the literal '-0' in a comparison expression with the literal '0'.
hazards: Rewriting '-0' to '0' inside a template literal changes the string value produced at runtime.
If '-0' appears as a property key (e.g., obj[-0]), replacing it with '0' alters the property name accessed due to key coercion differences.
When '-0' is used as a label in a labeled statement, substituting it with '0' creates a different label, breaking goto-like control flow via break/continue.
In a destructuring pattern like [-0] = arr, changing '-0' to '0' modifies the ignored element index, potentially affecting which values are skipped.
If '-0' is written as part of a numeric literal in a comment (e.g., // threshold: -0), the fix erroneously alters the comment text, misleading future readers.
When '-0' is embedded in a regular expression literal (e.g., /-0/), rewriting it to '/0/' changes the pattern matched, causing test or exec to behave differently.
In a tagged template literal like fn`-0`, substituting '-0' with '0' changes the cooked string value passed to the tag function, altering its output.
If '-0' occurs within a JSX text node (e.g., {-0}), replacing it with '0' changes the rendered string content in the DOM.
When '-0' is used as a hexadecimal escape in a string (e.g., '\x2d\x30'), the tool does not recognize it, so no rewrite occurs—but if it did, it would corrupt the escape sequence.
In WebAssembly text format embedded as a string (e.g., '(i32.const -0)'), rewriting '-0' to '0' changes the constant value, altering module semantics.
If '-0' is part of a URL or API endpoint string (e.g., `fetch('/api/-0')`), substituting it with '0' changes the resource requested, leading to 404 or wrong data.
When '-0' is used as a CSS unit or value in a style string (e.g., 'margin: -0px'), replacing it with '0' alters the computed style, though visually identical, it may affect CSSOM property access.
